items.title: Sub-Part 14: Why the Buddha Chose to Relinquish His Own Remaining Years

items.zh: 等不等而生，牟尼捨有行。內樂定差別，如俱舍卵生。
items.en: Equal, yet unequal, in what arose — the sage relinquished the formations of existence. Through the distinction of inner joy and concentration, it was like a chick breaking from its shell.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂佛示現住最後有菩薩位時，先所獲得三十有二大丈夫相，八十隨好圓滿莊嚴妙色身生，於後證得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提時，其色身生與前正等。其名身生，由勝無漏不相似故，與前不等。又佛示現內寂靜樂、及沙門樂、為依止故，得定自在；如定心力，捨諸壽行及諸有行。彼捨邊際妙色身生，與前正等。其名身生與前不等，故有差別。如因其㲉卵生雞等，依卵而生，即此生已，漸漸增長，種類相似，破㲉而出。如是如來色身、名身差別道理，當知亦爾。此中差別，謂佛世尊若不棄捨諸壽行者，應滿壽量方般涅槃。定力所持，捨壽行故，不滿壽量而般涅槃。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，捨諸壽行，色身、名身二種差別，及顯棄捨所依因緣。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: This verse explains the following. When the Buddha manifested dwelling in the stage of a bodhisattva in his last existence, the birth of his body of form, the wonderful form body perfectly adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor marks that he had previously attained, was, when he later realised unsurpassed perfect awakening, exactly equal to what it had been before. The birth of his name body, however, was not equal to what it had been before, because the superior untainted [qualities] are dissimilar to what came before. Again, the Buddha manifested that, relying on the inner happiness of peace and the happiness of the ascetic, he attained mastery of concentration, and by the power of the concentrated mind relinquished the formations of life and the formations of existence. The birth of the wonderful form body at that final point of relinquishing was exactly equal to what it had been before; the birth of the name body was not equal to what it had been before; hence there is a difference. Just as a chick and the like are born from an egg, depending on the egg for their birth, and once born gradually grow, being similar in kind, and break out of the shell, so too should the principle of the difference between the Tathāgata's form body and name body be understood. The distinction here is that if the Buddha, the World-Honoured One, had not relinquished the formations of life, he would have entered final nirvana only on completing his lifespan; because, sustained by the power of concentration, he relinquished the formations of life, he entered final nirvana without completing his lifespan. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows the relinquishing of the formations of life, the two kinds of difference between the form body and the name body, and the cause and condition on which the relinquishing depends. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Sub-Part 15: Mud, Demons, Nets, and Rivers — Four Images for Four Afflictions

items.zh: 無淤泥等欲，無魑魅等瞋；無羅網等癡，無江河等愛。
items.en: Let there be no craving like sinking mud; no aversion like a hostile spirit; no delusion like an entangling net; no attachment like a rushing river.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂有四種能為世俗不自在法，世間現見能令有情不自在轉。一者、陷溺淤泥；二者、鬼魅所著；三者、入於羅網；四者、墮駛流河，隨流漂溺。復有四種能為真實不自在法，能令有情不自在轉，當知亦爾。何等為四？謂如有一，生長欲界，陷溺不淨腥臊生臭諸欲淤泥，不能自在引發守護增長善法。又如有一，棄捨諸欲，於善說法毘奈耶中而得出家。心懷忿怒，性多惡言；由忿所持，不得自在；不數學處，動生違越；於諸智者同梵行所，屢以麁言擊刺、訶擯、侵惱、毀辱。又如有一，棄捨諸欲，於惡說法毘奈耶中而得出家，入諸惡魔大癡見網。彼既入已，流轉生死，不得自在。又如有一，生長上分諸離欲地，於諸愛結未能永斷，亦未遍知，不得自在，還生下界，順流而住，難可出離。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，諸界、諸品愚夫纏縛。復有差別。謂如有一，陷欲淤泥，不能自在於善說法毘奈耶中清淨出家。又如有一，為性忿怒，忿怒所蔽，憤恚纏心，尚於自身或害、或損，何況於他。又如有一，成就癡品諸惡邪見。謂無父母，毀謗父母，於父母所反悕敬養，況自能為。又如有一，廣集諸欲，貪愛所漂，不得自在；尚不欲自食，況能惠於他。如是四法，當知能障諸聰慧者四應知法。謂善說法毘奈耶中清淨出家、遠離恚害、敬事父母、樂行慧施。
items.en: This verse explains the following. There are four conventional things that make one unfree, which are seen in the world to make beings unable to act freely: first, sinking into mud; second, being possessed by a ghost or demon; third, being caught in a net; fourth, falling into a swift river and being swept along and drowned. It should be understood that there are likewise four real things that make one unfree, which make beings unable to act freely. What are the four? Someone born and raised in the desire realm sinks into the mud of sense pleasures, impure, rank and foul-smelling, and cannot freely bring about, guard and increase wholesome qualities. Again, someone gives up sense pleasures and goes forth in the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, but harbours anger in their heart and is by nature given to harsh speech; held by anger, they are not free. They do not train in the points of training and readily transgress them; towards wise companions in the holy life they repeatedly use harsh words to sting, rebuke, expel, trouble and insult them. Again, someone gives up sense pleasures and goes forth in a badly proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, and enters the net of great delusion and wrong views of the evil Māra. Having entered it, they wander on in birth-and-death and are not free. Again, someone born and raised in the higher stages free from desire has not yet cut off for ever, nor yet fully understood, the fetters of craving; they are not free, are reborn again in the lower realm, abide going with the stream, and find it hard to escape. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows the bondage of fools in all realms and of all classes. There is a further distinction. Someone sinks into the mud of sense desire and cannot freely go forth in purity in the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya. Again, someone is by nature angry; covered over by anger, with resentment entangling their mind, they harm or injure even themselves, let alone others. Again, someone possesses the evil wrong views belonging to the class of delusion, namely that there is no father and mother; slandering their father and mother, they instead expect respect and support from their father and mother, let alone being able to provide these themselves. Again, someone accumulates sense pleasures widely and, swept along by greed and craving, is not free; they do not even wish to eat themselves, let alone give to others. It should be understood that these four things obstruct four things that the intelligent ought to know: going forth in purity in the well-proclaimed Dharma and Vinaya, keeping far from anger and harm, respectfully serving father and mother, and delighting in practising wise generosity.

blocks.text: Two verses. The first concerns the Buddha's decision to enter final nirvāṇa at eighty. Both explanations are **missing from Ru-Yi's translation**; the English column gives our own translation.

subs.head: The sage relinquishes the formations of existence

blocks.text: "Equal, yet unequal, in what arose, the sage relinquished the formations of existence. Through inner joy and concentration, it was like a chick breaking from its shell."

The prose: the Buddha's **form body** after awakening was "equal" to the bodhisattva's before it, with the same thirty-two marks. His **name body**, his mind, was "unequal": utterly transformed by supreme uncontaminated wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: the body did not change; the inner vision did. Through mastery of concentration, the Buddha relinquished his remaining life-formations, as a chick that grew inside the egg breaks out of the shell. Had he not done so, he would have lived out his full span. Venerable Miào Jìng: a life of a hundred years has five twenty-year portions; the Buddha lived four and relinquished the fifth.
"Let there be no craving like sinking mud; no aversion like a hostile spirit; no delusion like an entangling net; no attachment like a rushing river."

The prose: four things in the world take away a person's freedom: sinking in mud, possession by a spirit, being caught in a net, being swept away by a river. Four things do the same to the mind: - A householder sunk in the "mud" of sense desire cannot develop the good. - A renunciant who is angry and harsh, "possessed" by anger, breaks the rules and abuses fellow practitioners. - A renunciant under a wrong teaching is caught in the "great net of deluded views". - One born in a higher realm who has not cut attachment is swept back down by the current. Venerable Miào Jìng: without the four foundations of mindfulness, sense craving was only suppressed.
A second reading: these four block four things the wise should know: going forth, freedom from hatred, honouring parents, and joyful giving.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "muni"?
options: the silent one — signifying freedom from affliction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: muni is also called "silent one" — in Chinese, 寂默 — meaning one without affliction.

quiz.q: "如俱舍卵生" is rendered "like a chick breaking from its shell." How do the lectures explain 俱舍 and the shell?
options: the shell is the physical body
Cháng Bǎi: kośa originally means a cocoon, and the shell stands for ignorance; Miào Jìng: unsurpassed awakening's aggregates do not cease, so it "breaks out of the shell"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: kośa is a transliteration with two meanings — originally, in Indian usage, a silkworm's cocoon; the shell stands for ignorance, in the sense of covering. Venerable Miào Jìng: the aggregates of unsurpassed awakening do not cease — hence "breaking out of the shell." The chick is an extended sense; the note's reading of the shell as the physical body differs from the *Pixunji*.

quiz.q: Which portion of his lifespan did the Buddha relinquish, per Venerable Miào Jìng following the Vibhāṣā?
options: taking twenty years as a portion, a hundred years is five; living to eighty he used four, relinquishing the fifth
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: taking twenty years as one portion, a hundred years has five; the Buddha lived only to eighty, using four portions — so he relinquished the fifth. He also notes another view based on 120 years.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "equal" in "equal yet unequal in what arose"?
options: the physical body before and after unsurpassed awakening did not change — it is equal
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the physical body before and after attaining unsurpassed awakening did not change — the body is the same, hence "equal." What is unequal is the inner virtue.

quiz.q: Which four images does the fifteenth verse use for four afflictions?
options: craving like mud, aversion like a demon, delusion like a net, attachment like a river
quiz.why: "Let there be no craving like sinking mud; no aversion like a hostile spirit; no delusion like an entangling net; no attachment like a rushing river." Master Cháng Bǎi: mud and the like are nominal designations; craving, aversion, delusion, and attachment are the real things that deprive one of freedom.

quiz.q: To which four kinds of people does Master Cháng Bǎi assign the four lines?
options: craving: lay ordinary people; aversion: ordinary monastics in this teaching; delusion: non-Buddhist renunciants; attachment: ordinary people with concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first, craving like mud, refers to worldly lay people; the second, aversion, to ordinary monastics within the Buddha's order; the third, delusion, to non-Buddhist renunciants; the fourth, attachment, to ordinary people who have concentration.

quiz.q: In "delusion like a net," who does Venerable Miào Jìng say the net-spreading "demon" is?
options: those who spread wrong views — their wrong views are the great net of deluded views
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the "evil demon" here refers to people who spread wrong knowledge and views; the wrong views they proclaim are "the great net of deluded views."
